Bank Holiday Motorcycle Routes

Bank holiday weekends offer precious long weekends for motorcycle touring. With three days to play with, you can reach areas that a standard weekend can't cover. But bank holidays also bring heavy traffic — here's how to make the most of them.

UK Bank Holidays 2026

  • New Year: January 1
  • Good Friday/Easter Monday: April dates (check annually)
  • Early May: First Monday in May
  • Late May (Spring): Last Monday in May
  • Late August (Summer): Last Monday in August
  • Christmas/Boxing Day: December 25-26

Route Strategies for Bank Holidays

  • Leave Friday evening: Get ahead of Saturday traffic. Ride 100 miles in the evening to your first overnight and start the weekend with a head start.
  • Return Monday evening: The worst traffic is Monday afternoon on motorways heading south. Return late or stay an extra night and ride home Tuesday morning.
  • Go against the flow: If everyone heads to the Lake District (south to north), ride the Scottish Borders (north to south). Counter-flow routes are emptier.

Best Bank Holiday Routes

Easter (3-4 days):

  • North Wales Loop: Chester → Snowdonia → Aberystwyth → Brecon Beacons → Chester (400 miles)
  • Devon and Cornwall: Bristol → Exmoor → Bodmin Moor → Land's End → Jurassic Coast → Bristol (500 miles)

May Bank Holidays (3 days):

  • Yorkshire Grand Tour: Leeds → Dales → North York Moors → Whitby → return (350 miles)
  • Scottish Borders: Edinburgh → Tweed Valley → Kielder → Northumberland Coast → Edinburgh (350 miles)

August Bank Holiday (3 days):

  • Peak District and Lake District: Sheffield → Peak District → Manchester → Lake District → return (400 miles)
  • Channel Islands: Poole → Guernsey → Jersey → Poole (ferry + island riding)
The key to a great bank holiday tour: leave early, avoid motorways, book accommodation in advance, and don't try to cover too many miles. A relaxed 150 miles per day on great roads beats 250 miles of motorway frustration every time.

Essential Bank Holiday Planning

Book your accommodation at least four weeks before any bank holiday weekend. Popular touring areas sell out completely during these periods, and last-minute options are typically limited to expensive hotels or inconveniently located properties. If you are flexible about your exact destination, consider booking two or three potential accommodations and cancelling the unused ones within their free cancellation windows.

Pack your motorcycle the evening before departure day. A Friday evening start gets you ahead of the Saturday morning traffic exodus, and every minute saved on departure morning is a minute of extra riding time on quiet roads. Have your route loaded on your GPS device, your fuel tank completely full, and all your gear laid out ready. A bank holiday weekend is precious riding time — don't waste any of it on avoidable logistics and last-minute preparation.

Consider building an itinerary that goes deliberately against the prevailing crowd flow. On a May bank holiday when everyone heads south towards the coast, ride north to the empty upland hills instead. On an August bank holiday when Cornwall and the Lake District are packed with tourists, the Scottish Borders and North Pennines remain gloriously empty and perfectly rideable. Leave Friday evening and return Monday evening or Tuesday morning to dodge the worst motorway congestion heading south.
Ride against the crowd flow: when everyone heads north to the Lakes, the Scottish Borders and North Pennines stay empty.
Book accommodation at least four weeks ahead for popular touring areas, which sell out completely over bank holidays.
Aim for a relaxed 150 miles a day on great roads rather than 250 miles of motorway frustration.

faq.q: When are the 2026 UK bank holidays?
faq.a: England and Wales have New Year (Jan 1), Good Friday (Apr 3), Easter Monday (Apr 6), the early May Monday (May 4), the spring Monday (May 25), the late August Monday (Aug 31), Christmas Day (Dec 25), and the Boxing Day substitute (Mon Dec 28). Scotland and Northern Ireland vary slightly, adding dates such as 2 January and St Andrew's Day.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book for a bank holiday tour?
faq.a: Book accommodation at least four weeks before any bank holiday weekend. Popular touring areas such as the Lake District, Snowdonia, and the Highlands sell out completely, leaving only expensive hotels or awkwardly located properties. If you are flexible, reserve two or three options with free cancellation and release the ones you do not use.

faq.q: How do I avoid the worst bank holiday traffic?
faq.a: Leave Friday evening to get ahead of the Saturday exodus, and return late Monday or on Tuesday morning to miss the southbound motorway crush. Ride against the prevailing flow: when everyone heads to Cornwall or the Lakes, the Scottish Borders and North Pennines stay gloriously quiet.

faq.q: Which bank holiday is best for a first tour of the year?
faq.a: Easter, with four days from Good Friday to Easter Monday, is the traditional season opener. The weather is unpredictable, so pack for winter and hope for spring, but the long weekend is ideal for a shakedown tour after the cold months.
